collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks a child aged 4-10 and an adult; in the story (name1) has an extra finger on each hand)

collection.description: A child with six fingers on each hand counts to twelve when everyone else stops at ten: make it a game, or ask about it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) was born with six fingers on each hand. (subject.He/she) has never thought much about it, until today, when (friend) is teaching the children to count on their fingers, and (subject) gets to twelve while everyone else stops at ten.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "Twelve?" says (friend). "Well, you're the best counter we've got." The other children all want to count to twelve too. They borrow sticks, toes and each other's fingers. It becomes a game: who can count highest using only what's in front of them. (subject) wins with fingers alone, and is extremely smug about it until dinner.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) asks if the extra fingers are useful. (subject) thinks hard. "Holding more mangoes." (subject.He/she) demonstrates. It's true; (subject.he/she) can hold one more mango than anyone else. (friend) declares (subject.him/her) the village Mango Carrier. (subject) takes the job very seriously, and for a week every mango in the village is carried by (subject.him/her), personally.
